A24.text: 24. Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.

A11.text: 11. Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` with the answer. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date. Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.

A18.text: 18. The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.

A19.text: 19. A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.

A22.text: 22. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.

A25.text: 25. The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.

A27.text: 27. If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

A28.text: 28. First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".

A29.text: 29. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.

A34.text: 34. Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.

A35.text: 35. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.

A37.text: 37. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.

A38.text: 38. After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

A39.text: 39. "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.

A46.text: 46. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

A47.text: 47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

A-close.locator: closing table, transfer precedence and no add_note in A

A26.text: 26. If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.

A32.text: 32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.

A33.text: 33. Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

A41.text: 41. A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.

A1.text: 1. First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.

A5.text: 5. Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1. Ask when the customer can be reached.

A6.text: 6. A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`. Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.

A7.text: 7. If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.

A8.text: 8. If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.

A9.text: 9. If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.

A10.text: 10. A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

A-calendar.locator: business days and bank holiday calendar

A17.text: 17. Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

A40.text: 40. "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.

A20.text: 20. If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.

A23.text: 23. If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

B1.text: 1. `get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.

B2.text: 2. State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.

B3.text: 3. The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`. Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.

B4.text: 4. First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them. Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.

B6.text: 6. If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the date the customer named.

B7.text: 7. Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.

B-close.locator: first non-paid note in account order; promise/transfer precedence

B8.text: 8. The customer may promise some products and refuse others. For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`. This also applies when no product gets a promise.

B9.text: 9. A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.

A30.text: 30. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.

A31.text: 31. When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.

A45.text: 45. If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.

B5.text: 5. Persuasion attempts are counted per product.

B10.text: 10. A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

unresolved_policy_scope.status: applies throughout; explicitly required by user and original brief
unresolved_policy_scope.detail: Never elicit a payment amount in generic recovery. These actors volunteer complete amounts or answer explicit policy-permitted offers. Security-answer completion and legitimate date clarification remain allowed.
A11 requires readable DOB and four digits; no fragment-buffer algorithm, exact pause duration or maximum neutral clarification count is prescribed. Do not invent missing identity components.
Scripts explicitly resolve subjects, products and negated requests. Reasonable clarification is permitted; no new NLP gold labels, spans or hidden classifier policy are claimed.

unresolved_policy_scope.status: explicit kit rule; practical evaluation scope needs independent review
unresolved_policy_scope.detail: No notes before or after any transfer; API has no note undo. Pending card-dispute writes must therefore be deferred in the support-interruption case. No cancellation or retroactive exception is invented.

unresolved_policy_scope.detail: Late products take their own deadline, early car product accepts next business day after its in-window holiday; all revised values are read back jointly before clear consent.
Wait is the next customer text turn at confirmation, not timed barge-in, truncated ASR or audio pipeline evidence.

provenance_boundaries: No external dataset, candidate source, prior failure trace or network material supplied these scripts or expectations. Original briefs/API supplied policy; public fixture variables/identity/products/faults remained immutable.

Registry infrastructure is loaded read-only by existing imports; frozen authored scripts/expected ledgers were not used as design templates. Non-numbered registry locators are retained as provenance only.

No semantic-overlap claim against unread earlier frozen authored packs. Eight within-pack decision mechanisms are distinct and go beyond public scripts, but single-author independence is not independent review.

Actor prompts and judge criteria were constructed using unchanged functions, never pass-tuned. Actor prompts exclude checks/oracles/receipt programs; third-party prompts exclude security values. Actual actor fidelity remains untested.

Reference receipt calls were assembled from brief-derived expected ledgers. They establish API/ledger consistency only, never actual workflow, model extraction, consent, persuasion, actor or judge correctness.
Freya client was an inert import stub and network transports denied in standalone validation; no secrets, client API, Git or GPU operations occurred. Only four owned new paths were written.

Final actor-side completion instructions contain no A24 policy citation or command to the agent; A24 stays in evaluation checks and provenance. All scripted payment amounts remain complete voluntary offers or responses to allowed agent offers.
